title: VPC DNS hostnames and resolver behavior
hook: AmazonProvidedDNS resolves hostnames inside your VPC — including AWS service endpoints and EC2 public DNS names when enabled. The resolver lives at the VPC network address plus two, for example 10.0.0.2 for a 10.0.0.0/16 VPC.

blocks.text: Every VPC has enableDnsSupport (default true) and enableDnsHostnames (default true for default VPC, false for custom unless set). With DNS support, instances use AmazonProvidedDNS at base of VPC CIDR + 2. AWS resolves public hostnames for EC2 with public IPs when hostnames enabled, and private DNS names for instances. Route 53 private hosted zones associate with VPC for custom internal names like api.internal.example.com.

entries.plainDefinition: AWS-managed DNS at VPC CIDR base + 2 address.
Allows VPC to use AWS DNS resolution.
entries.example: Must be true for RDS endpoint hostname resolution.

entries.plainDefinition: Assigns public DNS hostnames to instances with public IPs.
DNS zone visible only inside associated VPCs.
entries.example: db.internal resolves to RDS private IP.

blocks.text: Applications reference RDS and ElastiCache by DNS endpoint — broken VPC DNS means connection failures despite correct security groups. Hybrid setups need Route 53 Resolver rules to forward on-prem names. Interviewers ask how a private EC2 resolves an S3 VPC endpoint DNS name.

blocks.title: Interview framing
blocks.body: Say: DNS at VPC+2, enableDnsSupport for AWS endpoints, private hosted zones for custom internal names, Resolver for hybrid.

sections.heading: How it works step by step

items.title: Instance queries VPC+2
items.body: DHCP option set assigns AmazonProvidedDNS to instances.

items.title: AWS service names
items.body: Resolver returns private IPs for RDS, ELB, and interface endpoint names.

items.title: Private zone
items.body: Associated Route 53 private zone answers custom internal records.

items.title: Hybrid forward
items.body: Resolver inbound/outbound endpoints forward corp.example.com to on-prem DNS.

diagram.title: VPC DNS resolution
diagram.source:
flowchart LR
  EC2[EC2 instance] -->|query| DNS[VPC+2 AmazonProvidedDNS]
  DNS --> RDS[RDS endpoint private IP]
  DNS --> PHZ[Route 53 private zone]
  DNS --> FWD[Resolver forward to on-prem]
  PHZ --> APP[api.internal → 10.0.10.50]

snippet.label: Enable VPC DNS attributes
snippet.code:
AppVpc:
  Type: AWS::EC2::VPC
  Properties:
    CidrBlock: 10.0.0.0/16
    EnableDnsSupport: true
    EnableDnsHostnames: true
InternalZone:
  Type: AWS::Route53::HostedZone
  Properties:
    Name: internal.example.com
    VPCs:
      - VPCId: !Ref AppVpc
        VPCRegion: !Ref AWS::Region
ApiRecord:
  Type: AWS::Route53::RecordSet
  Properties:
    HostedZoneId: !Ref InternalZone
    Name: api.internal.example.com
    Type: A
    TTL: "60"
    ResourceRecords:
      - 10.0.10.50
snippet.explanation: Private zone only resolves inside associated VPC. C# app uses https://api.internal.example.com with cert from ACM private CA or internal PKI.

snippet.label: Verify DNS settings on VPC
snippet.code:
aws ec2 describe-vpc-attribute --vpc-id vpc-0abc123 --attribute enableDnsSupport
aws ec2 describe-vpc-attribute --vpc-id vpc-0abc123 --attribute enableDnsHostnames
snippet.explanation: Both should be true for standard app VPC. False enableDnsSupport breaks AWS endpoint resolution.

snippet.label: Test resolution from instance
snippet.explanation: First resolves RDS to private IP. Second confirms private zone via VPC resolver.

blocks.title: VPC DNS vs Active Directory DNS
rows: SRV records or hardcoded SQL hostname
Connection string uses RDS DNS endpoint

blocks.title: Pitfalls to avoid
blocks.body: enableDnsSupport false on custom VPC. Private hosted zone not associated with VPC. Custom DHCP option set pointing to wrong DNS without forwarders. Hardcoding RDS IP instead of endpoint — fails on failover.

blocks.text: How to prove it in production: query logging on Route 53 Resolver; dig from bastion via SSM; verify split-horizon — same name public vs private zone. Interface VPC endpoints create private DNS names — enablePrivateDnsName on endpoint or apps must use correct suffix. Hybrid: Resolver rules FORWARD corp.example.com to on-prem IP; INBOUND endpoint lets on-prem resolve AWS private zones.

blocks.title: Tradeoffs at senior level
rows: Less control than full custom DNS
Single point of failure if link down
Breaks on RDS failover — rejected pattern

blocks.title: What gets you rejected in interviews
blocks.body: Saying DNS is 'just Route 53' without VPC resolver at +2. Strong answer: AmazonProvidedDNS for AWS names, private zones for custom, Resolver for hybrid, always use RDS endpoint hostname in connection strings.

interviewTakeaways: AmazonProvidedDNS at VPC network address + 2 resolves AWS service endpoints inside the VPC.
enableDnsSupport and enableDnsHostnames must be true for standard EC2 and RDS hostname behavior.
Route 53 private hosted zones provide custom internal names associated with VPC.
60s: DNS at VPC+2. RDS endpoint hostname not IP. Private zone for internal apps. Resolver for hybrid forward.
Follow-up: how does private DNS work for interface VPC endpoints?
commonPitfalls: Hardcoding database IP gets you rejected — use RDS DNS endpoint for failover.
Strong answer: VPC+2 resolver, enableDns flags, private zone association.
Private hosted zone in wrong Region association — silent resolution failure.
Disabling enableDnsSupport and wondering why ELB hostname does not resolve.

jsTsCorrelations.note: Node apps use ElastiCache configuration endpoint hostname — DNS failure looks like ETIMEDOUT same as C# StackExchange.Redis pointing at wrong static IP.
TypeScript microservices in EKS use CoreDNS plus optional private zones — analogous to C# services registering in Consul or AD DNS on-prem.
